question.text: Arjun Mehta, a portfolio manager at a Mumbai PMS, tracks the NIFTY 50 by holding all 50 stocks in their exact index weights and rebalances when NSE publishes constituent changes. Which indexing technique is he using?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Full Replication holds every constituent in the same (or near-same) weight as the index — recommended when the index has few, liquid stocks like NIFTY 50. **The Trap:** Sampling replaces some constituents with similar stocks; used when full replication is costly (e.g., NIFTY 500). Smart Beta uses rule-based factor tilts, not pure index mirroring. **Cross-Exam Context:** XXI-A covered the same indexing techniques conceptually; XXI-B expects you to pick the right technique for a given index size and liquidity. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Full replication minimises tracking error but demands AUM scale. For NIFTY 500-type indices, sampling is the practical route.
